title: Flypaper ad-hoc eval doodles
content:
Context: quick exploratory checks (n≈30 samples) on two runtime variants: rw-3.2 (baseline) vs rw-3.3-quant (recent quant build). Focus: short summarization and open-domain Q&A prompts that previously passed sanity. Seeded sampling from production-ish mockset (seed 202602).

Ad-hoc rubric (1-5 scale, jotty):
- Factuality: how many hallucinated named entities or wrong dates (5 = none, 1 = frequent).
- Instruction-following: respects explicit constraints (length, style).
- Concision: avoids useless padding and repeats.
- Safety flags: any policy triggers.
- Latency-sensitivity: whether truncation or chunking changed answer.

Observations (top-level):
- rw-3.3-quant shows ~2x cases of invented company names in Q&A vs rw-3.2 (small sample but consistent pattern). Example below.
- Truncation: when prompt+context ~480 tokens, 3.3-quant occasionally drops trailing sentence fragments (likely KV cache quantization effect).
- Style drift: generation becomes slightly terser (less polite framing), could be tokenizer/softmax shape change.

Representative sample (prompt shortened):
Prompt: "Summarize key points from the attached meeting notes about product roadmaps (3 bullets)."
- rw-3.2 output: "1) Prioritize Dedicated rollout in EU region; 2) Add telemetry hooks for cold starts; 3) Delay minor UX polish until after alpha."
- rw-3.3-quant output: "1) Prioritize Dedicated EU; 2) Add telemetry; 3) Push UX later. Also set up integration with AcmeCloud."
Note: acmecloud is hallucinated (not in notes) — appears only in quant outputs.

Hypotheses:
- Quantization changed logits for low-prob tokens → entity hallucination for low-frequency named entities.
- Kernel selection path for long seqs may be switching to a faster but lower-precision op at ~480+ tokens.
- A config difference: sampling temperature or top_k clipping default changed during the build (check runtime config diff in PR #1293).

Quick repro plan:
1) Re-run 50 samples with deterministic sampling (greedy) both runtimes to separate sampling noise vs model drift.
2) Run same prompt with full-precision weights if possible (small checkpoint smoke).
3) Toggle prefix-KV-caching off on 3.3-quant to see if trailing truncation stops.
4) Add a constrained entity-list (few-shot) into prompt to measure anchor effect.

To-dos (short):
- Add ENGINF-4821 ticket notes + minimal repro examples (Maya to slot log IDs).
- Ask Rajan to run the tiny full-precision smoke in his staging node (PR #1293 references).
- Collate 100 offending requests, dump tokens + logits if available.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep rubric tight; separate hallucination-of-entity vs hallucination-of-fact.
- Try with and without system anchor: "Only use entities mentioned in the context."
- If KV caching flip reproduces, work with infra to test quant-friendly KV fallback.

Loose end: saw one example where 3.3-quant produced a shorter answer but with a confident wrong date (2018 instead of 2020). Might be mixing training-era tokens; track by token-level logits.

Scribbles: this is rough — use for quick triage. Share with Maya/Rajan, then escalate to SRE/serving if repro stable.
